content: Soon after initiating HIV treatment or even months later, changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication. These changes can include an increase in fat in the upper back and abdominal areas, as well as a decrease in fat in the arms and legs. The exact cause and long-term effects of these changes remain unknown. Efavirenz commonly causes a rash, which is usually not severe. In adults, this rash may appear within the first two weeks of starting treatment and typically resolves within four weeks if it is not serious. In children, a rash may develop within the first four weeks of treatment. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this rash from a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. In the United States, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, also contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking efavirenz, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Efavirenz may lead to a condition affecting heart rhythm known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase the risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be heightened if you use certain medications, such as diuretics (water pills), or if you experience conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This drug may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or difficulty concentrating. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. Rashes may be more common and severe in children taking efavirenz. Report any rash immediately. A doctor may prescribe an antihistamine for your child to take before starting efavirenz. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. HIV treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting the infection to your baby, and efavirenz may be part of that treatment. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications can affect the removal of efavirenz from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Efavirenz can also accelerate the removal of many other medications from your body, which may affect their efficacy. Certain other drugs used to treat HIV infection, such as elvitegravir or other NNRTIs (including etravirine, nevirapine, or rilpivirine), may interact with efavirenz. If you are taking atazanavir with this medication, you may also need to take another medication, such as ritonavir. Efavirenz may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. Check the labels on all your medications, including allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine cannabinoid tests, potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as liver function tests, viral load, T-cell counts, cholesterol, and triglyceride levels, should be conducted before starting this medication and while taking it. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
